Seeded 2026-11-23 from the KPI scoreboard in workspace/goals/global-startup-tracking/hidden_files/process-critique-and-kpis-2026-11-23.md; every candidate was checked against the live open-issue list for castlemilk/startup-atlas so nothing duplicates a filed issue.

entries.body:
## Problem

The pipeline is fast (about 12 minutes of machine work) but the loop is slow because nearly every step is a manual or browser-mediated action by the operator: dispatch via the browser, artifact download + review, corpus publishes, manual indexer trigger, the 151-file console deploy loop, and browser query verification.

## Evidence (23 Nov 2026, crawl #43)

- Crawl run 45107803260: 2m 55s machine time.
- Indexer execution td5zx: 8.53s.
- Verified browser queries: 8 ms / 24 ms once the engine loaded.
- Total wall-clock for the full loop: ~2 hours.
- Target (KPI F3): under 30 minutes, mostly review.

## Proposed fix

Automate the remaining manual steps: the console deploy as a build/publish step instead of a manual 151-file upload loop, and a one-command (task target or CLI) path for the corpus publish + indexer trigger instead of console clicks and manual REST calls. Dispatch via `gh workflow run` where the VM can reach it.

## Notes

- Issue #376 covers one of the manual steps (auto-publish the reviewed corpus on data/ changes); this ticket covers the remaining steps, not that trigger.
- Source: process-critique-and-kpis-2026-11-23.md, finding P1 and ranked improvement #1.
entries.title: Automate the manual loop steps so wall-clock drops from ~2 h toward 30 min

entries.body:
## Problem

No check tracks how old the reviewed files are. The stalest dataset goes unnoticed until someone happens to look at it.

## Evidence (23 Nov 2026)

- Oldest unchecked dataset: `data/partner-profiles.json`, last checked 12–13 Nov 2026 — 10 days old at the time of measurement.
- Target (KPI F4): under 7 days.
- The loop health check (issue #375) covers crawl conclusion, index version age, corpus-vs-main lag and console query success — but not per-file checked dates, so this gap is invisible to it.

## Proposed fix

Record a `checked` date per reviewed file, and have the loop health check report the stalest file and its age, flagging it the day it passes 7 days.

## Notes

- Distinct from #375 (health check + console smoke test), which does not cover per-file freshness.
- Source: process-critique-and-kpis-2026-11-23.md, KPI F4.
entries.title: Flag the stalest reviewed dataset: partner-profiles.json unchecked for 10 days

entries.body:
## Problem

The crawl reports per-source failures every run and still concludes "success". A dead source is discovered by reading an artifact, not by an alert.

## Evidence (crawl #41, 23 Nov 2026)

- Partners: 2/5 sources failed; programs: 4/17 failed; news: 1/4 failed.
- Canva 403s for the third consecutive run.
- 18/32 partners yield zero people rows on JS-rendered grids; 195 logo candidates dropped to the per-site limit.
- Target (KPI Q4): 0 failing sources, or flagged same-day.

## Proposed fix

Record per-source status (pages ok / 0 pages / failed) in the run summary and in the crawl registry (`data/crawl-runs.json`), and flag same-day when a source returns 0 pages ok. This is the crawl-engine review's proposal R12 and the process critique's improvement #10.

## Notes

- Related, not a duplicate: #89 (old OPS-01 epic, "Measure source coverage, freshness and crawl health") is the broad epic; this ticket is the specific per-source-status implementation.
- Issue #356 (structured-JSON fetch for JS-rendered grids) is a different fix — it changes how grids are fetched, not how failures are surfaced.
- Source: process-critique-and-kpis-2026-11-23.md, finding P9 and ranked improvement #10; crawl-engine-deep-review-2026-11-23.md, proposal R12.
entries.title: Surface per-source status in the crawl run summary and registry
